text: Step two is roasting. The concentrate is heated in air in a reverberatory furnace at about ten seventy kelvin, below its melting point. Moisture goes, arsenic and antimony escape as volatile oxides, and the sulphides start to burn. Copper pyrite gives copper one sulphide and iron sulphide, and some of each is oxidised. Roasting is kept incomplete on purpose, because some copper sulphide is needed later.
